logp.method_description: In order to assess the potential relation between the hydrophobicity/lipophilicity of complexes and biological activity, partition coefficients (log Po/w) were determined in an octanol–water medium. Using the “shake flask” method, log Po/w values were calculated by assessing the ratio of equilibrium concentration between the n-octanol (organic) and water (aqueous) phase. The log Po/w values show that complex 1 has a value of 1.24 ± 0.04, complex 2 has 1.13 ± 0.02, and complex 3 has 1.01 ± 0.05, indicating that complexes 1 and 2 are more hydrophobic than complex 3. They follow the trend in the order of 1 > 2 > 3, and this difference likely results from the thiophene group present in the ligand backbone of complexes 1 and 2, which increases their hydrophobic nature compared to complex 3. However, complex 1 has the highest hydrophobicity in the series, which is probably due to the –OCH2CH3 group (in the ligand skeleton), which may enhance the hydrophobicity of the complex.
